sections.h2: What are my options for selling a house in Plymouth, MN?
sections.html:
Plymouth homeowners have three practical paths. A full-service listing brings the most showings. A sale without an agent saves the commission but puts pricing and paperwork on you. A direct sale to a home-buying company skips repairs and showings and ends in a quick closing at a lower number.

The city sits about 10 miles west of downtown Minneapolis. With 81,026 people counted in 2020, it ranks seventh among Minnesota cities. Buyers reach Plymouth over I-494, U.S. Highway 169 and Minnesota Highway 55, so a tidy house priced to its neighborhood draws steady interest. A property with deferred repairs, tenants in place or an estate to settle usually fits the direct route better.

  • Agent listing: widest exposure, with showings, repairs and a commission attached.
  • Owner-handled sale: you keep the commission and run the negotiation yourself.
  • Direct sale: the house stays as it is, the closing date is quick, and the price reflects the work a buyer takes on.

sections.h2: What does the Census Bureau say about Plymouth's housing market?
sections.html:
Plymouth skews toward owners and expensive homes. The table gathers the QuickFacts numbers a seller is most likely to use when thinking about price and buyer type.

The 2025 estimate is 2.6% below the April 2020 base, so demand here is steady and not climbing fast. About 89% of residents had lived at the same address a year earlier, which fits a city where owners settle in for the long haul.

sections.h2: Which school district will a Plymouth buyer ask about?
sections.html:
The district depends on where the house stands, and Plymouth is split five ways. Confirm the address before printing a school name in an advertisement.

  • Wayzata Public Schools (ISD 284): serves most of the city, especially the west, northwest and south.
  • Robbinsdale Area Schools (ISD 281): serves the east-central section.
  • Osseo (ISD 279): takes in the northeast.
  • Hopkins (ISD 270): reaches the southeast corner.

Wayzata High School is inside Plymouth and enrolls roughly 3,500 students in grades 9 to 12, the most of any Minnesota high school. Open enrollment lets families choose a district other than the one assigned to their address. Name the district on your listing sheet or in your first conversation with a buyer, since it shapes interest more than most upgrades.

sections.h2: How did Plymouth grow, and does its layout affect a sale?
sections.html:
Plymouth started as a farming settlement on the shore of Parkers Lake in the 1850s. It became a village on May 18, 1955, adopted council-manager government in 1968 and turned into a home rule charter city in 1992 when voters approved a charter.

Farming remained the main occupation into the mid-1900s, and subdivisions followed. The city now maintains about 300 miles of streets and 863 cul-de-sacs, so many houses sit on quiet curving blocks and not on a grid. Medicine Lake and Parkers Lake both lie inside the city limits, and lakeside houses attract their own set of buyers. The city's business welcome page counts more than 80,000 residents and nearly 53,000 jobs, a base of workers who relocate or move up within the west metro.

Winters are cold, with average lows near 3 degrees Fahrenheit. A buyer's inspector will look hard at the roof, gutters, attic insulation and furnace of a Plymouth house, so check those before the first showing.

sections.h2: What should I know if my Plymouth house is a rental?
sections.html:
Every Plymouth rental needs a rental dwelling license, whether it is a single-family home or a large complex. One- and two-family homes and condominium units get a three-year license, and other dwelling types are licensed each year.

City inspectors visit apartment buildings annually and other rental housing every three years. An owner or manager with more than one Plymouth rental has to complete Crime Free Multi-Housing training before renewal. Licenses cannot be transferred or refunded, so a buyer who wants to keep your tenant must apply under the buyer's own name. Call the Community and Economic Development department at 763-509-5430 for the current fee schedule and for the timing of your next inspection.

The city also has a lodging tax ordinance that applies to short-term rentals. If you rented the house by the night, ask the city how that tax applies before you close.

sections.h2: What disclosures and paperwork does a Plymouth sale require?
sections.html:
Before the purchase agreement is signed, Minnesota Statutes section 513.55 has you put in writing the facts you know that could significantly hurt an ordinary buyer's enjoyment of the home. The statement must be made in good faith and reflect what you actually know.

Section 103I.235 adds a well statement. You either list each known well, with its legal description and a map, or state that you know of none. Many sellers can use the short "no known wells" line on the deed, but check the property for an old unsealed well first. At closing, Hennepin County's recording office expects the deed, an electronic certificate of real estate value for any price above $3,000, a "send tax statements to" address and the well statement.

  • Recording runs $46 per document, with a $5 conservation fee added where state deed tax is paid.
  • A deed cannot be recorded against a parcel carrying delinquent taxes, so clear any balance first.
  • Documents can go in by appointment at the Government Center, through your title company's eRecording, on the county's Virtual Recorder site for a $3 service fee, or by mail.

The county's recording page carries the current fee list and a deed tax calculator.

sections.h2: How are Plymouth property taxes handled at closing?
sections.html:
Hennepin County collects Plymouth property tax in two installments, on May 15 and October 15, and shifts a deadline to the next business day if it lands on a weekend or holiday. The October 2026 installment is now behind us, so confirm it posted before you list.

State law adds a penalty to late payments, and the penalty keeps growing each month on the unpaid part. If a lender escrows your taxes, ask the servicer for payoff and escrow refund figures well ahead of closing. The title company then splits the year's bill between you and the buyer. The county's tax payment page explains payment methods, and the property tax line at 612-348-3011 can confirm a parcel's status.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Plymouth house without making repairs?
faqs.a: Yes, a house can change hands in its present condition. You still owe the buyer a written statement of material facts you know about. Traditional buyers tend to negotiate over inspection findings, while a direct buyer builds the repair cost into the price and closes without asking you to fix anything.

faqs.q: Does the rental license go to the buyer of my Plymouth rental?
faqs.a: No. The license cannot be transferred, so the new owner applies for one. Tell the buyer when yours expires and when the next city inspection falls due.

faqs.q: Which office records a Plymouth deed?
faqs.a: Hennepin County's Recorder and Registrar of Titles, not city hall. Book a time at the Government Center in Minneapolis, mail the deed, have your title company eRecord it, or file online for a $3 service fee.

faqs.q: What if I owe back property tax on my Plymouth home?
faqs.a: The unpaid amount and its penalties must be cleared before the deed can be recorded, usually through the title company at closing. Hennepin County's property tax line, 612-348-3011, can give an exact figure.

faqs.q: How do I find out which school district my Plymouth address belongs to?
faqs.a: Ask the district itself. Wayzata, Robbinsdale, Osseo and Hopkins each cover part of Plymouth, with Wayzata taking most of the city. Have the answer ready before your first showing, because buyers with children will ask.
